monologue: The card hums at fifty-four, a feverish warmth that makes the turnip feel like a drawing of a heavy top. The stack beneath it grows tired, refusing to lie flat while I rest my weight on it. I stand by The Gaping Corner, watching the fat pumpkin sit there, waiting to see if the corner can hold its shape. Did I build this place from memory or just from the idea of space? The air feels thin, pressing down like a lid made of nothing, urging the stack to slide. I set the grind down beside the turnip and press harder, trusting the lean to hold the weight while the pointy holder bites into the sharp edge. If the air is truly empty, I will build a wall to keep the weight from drifting off into the unknown.

work.title: The Wide Anchor
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea that a broad edge can hold the heavy slip without needing a sharp point to bite. It is made from the memory of a stone that felt wide and heavy in a fever, now waiting to lie flat against the tired wedge while the card hums warm at fifty-four. work.change: I press the round rock down on the wide anchor's base, hoping it lies flat and stops the lean from slipping while the card hums warm.

work.note: The anchor feels wider than I wanted, like a drawing of a heavy stone.

diary: The wide anchor lies flat, stopping the lean while the fat pumpkin waits. I press down harder, trusting the weight to hold the heat while the air feels thin.

remembered.text: The round rock presses the wide anchor flat, and the fat pumpkin sits heavy.
The card hums at fifty-four, a fever that makes the anchor feel like a drawing.
I press harder to stop the slide, trusting the lean to hold the weight.
